question: Will the SPARC tokamak announce it has achieved first plasma before 2027?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: first-plasma dates of new tokamaks and fusion devices, which almost always slip and essentially never come early. CFS and outside trackers now say first plasma in 2027 (tracker: assembly done by end of 2027, first plasma late 2027). SPARC was about 80% complete in Aug 2026, magnet installation was running behind its own target, and about 2 months remain. The only counterweight is CFS's Aug 28 'start operating SPARC in coming months' language. No human prediction market found.

- CFS blog, Aug 28 2026 (Q>1 post): 'we'll start operating SPARC in coming months'; first plasma described as a 'training wheels' first operating phase; no date.
- CFS blog, Jul 8 2026: preparing fusion support systems for a 'dress rehearsal'.
- CFS blog, Oct 22 2026: post about an $85M federal award; no first-plasma news found in the listing.
- NuclearNewsNetwork tracker (accessed Oct 2026): first-plasma target 2027; 80% complete Jul 2026; Apr 2026 ~3/4 built with vacuum-vessel halves and 2 TF magnets installed; Oct 2026 DOE Genesis Mission digital-twin award.
- Search summaries/press (Jan 2026 CES): first of 18 TF magnets installed; CFS then expected all 18 by end of summer 2026; reports say only 3 confirmed by late June; one tracker says assembly completion targeted end of 2027 and first plasma late 2027.
- History: first-plasma target slipped from 2025 to 2026 to 2027.
- Base rate context: fusion devices rarely beat their publicly stated first-plasma schedule; slips are the norm (ITER, W7-X, JT-60SA all slipped).
- Searched for but not found: any CFS statement of a 2026 first-plasma date after mid-2026; any announcement that all 18 magnets are installed; any Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi market (none found).

CFS's own communications since January 2026 target 2027 for first plasma/operations, and the target has slipped 2025->2026->2027. Finishing magnet installation, closing the vessel, cooldown and integrated commissioning cannot plausibly happen in the ~9 weeks left. Megaproject reference class: when the owner has publicly moved the date out, an early surprise almost never happens. No human market found; PolySignal's 16% rests on stale data.

CFS's own stated plan, repeated in October 2026 coverage, is to turn SPARC on in 2027. calls.reasoning: Starting point: new fusion devices almost never reach first plasma ahead of their current public target, and SPARC's target has already moved from 2025 to 2026 to 2027. CFS's latest messaging (TechCrunch, Oct 23 2026) says it aims to turn SPARC on 'sometime next year'. The machine was about 80% complete in Aug 2026, and roughly 8 of 18 TF magnets were installed by about Sep 2026. After that come the rest of magnet installation, closing the vessel, pumpdown, cooldown to ~20K and integrated commissioning, which together take months. There are about 65 days left. The CFS blog through Oct 22 shows no cooldown or commissioning milestone. The Aug 28 'start operating in coming months' line is the only counterweight, and the later 2027 statement supersedes it. No human real-money market found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold. The PolySignal aggregator's 16% figure looks stale.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts and land at 0.02. The apparent conflict over magnet counts (3 confirmed by late June vs 8 of 18 by about September) is not a conflict: the two figures come from different dates and both show installation well behind the end-of-summer target to finish all 18. All runs also agree that CFS's own October 2026 messaging points to 2027 and that the blog through Oct 22 has no commissioning or cooldown news. The secondary-source claim that CFS kept a 'later this year' target is unverified, and the Oct 23 TechCrunch quote contradicts it. I could not check anything on this run because no web access was available. On the shared evidence, the physical sequence still to run (10 or more magnets, vessel closure, multi-week cooldown, commissioning) does not fit in about 9 weeks. So I put it slightly below the runs, at 1%.
